text:
Maya (People Ops): quick q — someone on Sam's team needs an emergency sick hours top-up during the year-end holiday window (accruals freeze). Can managers approve a one-time 8h top-up from the emergency sick pool? link to form: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/sick-topup :question:
Alex: is this FT headcount or a contractor? policy differs for contractors.
Priya: full-time EE, started 5 months ago, exhausted PTO after a family emergency. asking for partial-day coverage next week.
Jordan: afaik managers can request emergency top-ups but HR must sign off for year-end blackout exceptions. there's a short approval flow.
Maya (People Ops): right — short version: managers can initiate a request but approval requires People Ops + finance if it's outside accrual rules. i'll paste the relevant excerpt.
Maya (People Ops): `Emergency Sick Pool (3.4): Up to 16 hours may be granted per rolling 12 months for verified emergencies. Requests during accrual freeze require People Ops review; payments are charged to manager budget after finance approval.`
Sam (Manager): thanks — i'll file the request. do we need medical docs?
Maya (People Ops): we only need verification notes for >8h or recurring events. for a one-time 8h top-up, a manager attestation + employee note is fine.
Alex: ok. what's the turnaround? holiday window could delay approvals.
Maya (People Ops): typical turnaround 24-48h on business days. during the winter window add a day, so expect ~72h. if it's urgent ping me directly. :phone: 
Priya: filing now, thanks. i'll cc Sam on the form.
HRbot: new request submitted by Priya via /forms — Request ID #SR-2026-114. Status: Pending People Ops review.
Maya (People Ops): got it, i'll review and loop in finance if needed. Sam — please include the manager budget code in the form to speed approval. :thumbsup:
Sam (Manager): will do, thanks all.
